chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman whose husband dies while she is away from her home: where does she observe her waiting period (iddah)? He said: Wherever she wishes, provided she does not spend the night away from her home. Therefore, the meaning in these narrations is that we interpret them as being of the type of recommendation (istihbab), rather than obligation (farḍ) and compulsion (ijbar).

key_terms.الاسْتِحْبَابِ: Recommendation (a level of legal ruling below obligation)
key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا: The one from whom death has occurred (widow)

ai.seo_question: Where does a widow observe her waiting period if her husband dies while she is away from home?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the flexibility of the iddah period for a widow who is traveling or away from her marital home when her husband passes away. The Imam permits her to remain wherever she is, provided she does not sleep elsewhere, a condition scholars interpret as recommended (istihbab) rather than mandatory, highlighting the pragmatic approach to legal obligations in Shia jurisprudence.
